Unsure if this failure also occurs with 6.9.0-rc.

1. https://code.qt.io/cgit/qt/qtbase.git/commit/?h=6.9&id=64fd9edb2c5e935ffc58ce12434b582e32d4e93b


### Observed Behavior

Compiling fails with:

```
src/core/toxstring.cpp:93:47: error: no matching function for call to ‘QString::arg(const char32_t&, int, int, QChar)’
   93 |         cleaned += QStringLiteral("\\x%1").arg(c, 2, 16, QChar('0')).toStdU32String();
      |                                               ^
```


### Expected Behavior

Compiling succeeds without errors.


### Reproducibility

Always

### Operating System

Linux

### Operating System version/distro/name/etc.

Gentoo Linux

comment_data.body:
https://github.com/qt/qtbase/commit/563ed822f867c6c3040956017d4ca7f3795f172c

>[...]
>[ChangeLog][QtCore][Potentially Source-Incompatible Changes] The
QString::arg() overloads have been redesigned. Character-like types
(char, char16_t, char8_t, wchar_t (still subject to QTBUG-126054 at
the time of writing), char32_t) now always output the character, not
its numeric value. In particular, char16_t and char arguments now
match the string-ish arg() overload (and therefore don't provide a
`base` argument anymore. A backwards-compatible fix is to cast char,
char16_t, and wchar_t arguments to uint. This also fixes the ambiguity
errors you may have seen when using a char16_t as `fillChar`.
>[...]

Sounds like we have to cast the `c` argument in `QStringLiteral("\\x%1").arg(c, 2, 16, QChar('0')).toStdU32String();` from `char32_t` to an integer type, `uint32_t` perhaps?

Wanted to make a PR for this, but it doesn't look like Qt 5.9 has been released yet - [I don't see any tarballs of it](https://master.qt-project.org/archive/qt/). I don't want to make a PR against a non-released Qt version which might change this QString behavior before the release, so I suggest we just wait until Qt 5.9 is released. (It's also easier to test against the release tarballs because I can then reuse our docker CI scripts to build qTox locally, instead of figuring out how to adapt our docker script setup to build Qt from git just for a single PR.)

Yep, only 6.9.0-rc is out, here for example:

https://download.qt.io/development_releases/qt/6.9

Latest release target was today, but it's not Qt if it's not late... several times.  : ]

Definitely best to wait for the actual release.

Looks like the even latest date is now 2025-04-02 [1].

1. https://wiki.qt.io/Qt_6.9_Release

Should be fixed by #589.

(Not sure why this issue didn't close automatically with the commit containing `Fixes TokTok/qTox#585` being merged.)

Thank you!

> (Not sure why this issue didn't close automatically with the commit containing `Fixes TokTok/qTox#585` being merged.)

(I think I've wondered about that in the past myself, and feel like I found that GitHub only looks at the PR comment for those, not the actual commit... but I could be remembering wrong-like.)
